title: Wednesday, September 9, 2026

headline.title: Brent is over $100 for the first time since July, and the oil shock is starting to bleed into rates. Brent +2.96% to $100.82 and WTI +2.68% to $95.52 after fresh US strikes on Iranian tankers were followed by another Iranian missile barrage against a US facility in Jordan — a cycle of retaliation rather than a single headline. The 10-year is at 4.80%, VIX +4.33% to 16.40, and futures are lower across the board: S&P −0.38%, Dow −0.63%, Nasdaq −0.54%, Russell −0.52%.
headline.summary: And META is doing something violent in the other direction — +5.14% to 645.00. Tuesday it printed a Failed 2 Up, taking Friday's 617.46 high to 624.80 and closing 613.48 back below it; premarket is twenty dollars above that failed high, on analysts turning positive on its AI assistant. Everything else in mega-cap is offered — GOOGL −2.13%, INTC −2.05%, TSM −1.53%, AMZN −1.51%. Two days of catalyst risk sit inside this session: the Treasury buyback size at 10:00am CT, where the market wants a number well above the prior “at least $4B”, and Apple's iPhone launch at 12:00pm CT.

overview: The energy shock is no longer isolated, and that is the change from yesterday. Brent through $100.82 for the first time since July, with the 10-year up a basis point to 4.80% and VIX up 4.33% to 16.40 — oil is now raising the discount rate on the same growth assets that have been carrying the index. China's August data pushed the same way overnight: PPI +3.8% against 3.6% expected and core CPI +1.0% versus 0.9%, firmer beneath an in-line 0.8% headline, and hawkish remarks from an Australian central-bank official lifted September hike expectations there too. Europe is broadly weaker, the major eurozone indices down 0.75% to 1.0%, with utilities, energy and telecom the only groups holding up. Against that, the AI bid has not broken — it has narrowed further into hardware. The two dated events today are both binary and both in the middle of the session: the Treasury announces the maximum size of its buyback operation at 10:00am CT, where expectations in some corners reach $10B or more against prior guidance of “at least $4B”, and Apple takes the stage at 12:00pm CT with a foldable iPhone Ultra and $100-200 price increases on Pro models in question. President Trump speaks at 8:15pm CT.

setups: Tuesday was a Failed 2 Up — it took Friday's 617.46 high to 624.80, then closed 613.48 back underneath it. Premarket 645.00 is not a marginal reclaim; it is twenty dollars above the failed high and above every level of the prior two weeks, on analysts turning positive on the AI assistant. Over 624.80 voids the failure and turns it into a 2-2 reversal up, and that level is already through by a wide margin. The caution is the same one this book keeps writing: a 5% premarket gap in a mega cap is rarely available at the open, and the last four gaps of this shape — SNOW, GTLB, MRVL, ORCL — all gave back a meaningful part of it inside the session. The opening range is the reference, not the 645 print.

Tuesday broke Friday's 317.86 low to 314.90 and closed 316.22, still under it — a clean 2 Down and the fourth consecutive lower close. Premarket 315.26 has not reclaimed anything. Under 317.86 it stays broken. The launch is at 12:00pm CT: foldable iPhone Ultra, potential $2,000-2,500 pricing, and possible $100-200 increases on Pro models — Morgan Stanley's most-consequential-since-iPhone-X framing, which makes it a pricing-power test rather than a spec refresh. Four sessions of selling into its own event is the fact to weigh, and the answer to a pricing question arrives in the December quarter, not on stage today.

Tuesday was a 2 Up — it took Friday's 143.03 high to 146.23 and closed 146.03 near it. Premarket 148.90 clears that high. The catalyst is now cumulative and physical rather than a headline: fresh US strikes on Iranian tankers, then an Iranian missile barrage against a US facility in Jordan, with Brent +2.96% to $100.82 — the first print above $100 since July — and WTI +2.68% to $95.52. XLE +1.02% confirms alongside, with OXY +1.68%, XOM +1.30%, CVX +1.19%. Over 146.23 continues it. The Oman “safe route” headline remains the dated risk that ends this in one print.

bull: Analysts turning positive on the AI assistant. Tuesday was a Failed 2 Up — took 617.46 to 624.80 and closed 613.48 under it — and premarket is twenty dollars above that failed high. The only mega cap bid on a red morning.

Adjusted EPS $2.19 against $1.74, revenue $1.53B in line, same-store sales +2.2%. Raised the low end of the full-year profit and comp outlook and expanded the remaining buyback authorization to $700M — an earnings and capital-return beat on modest top-line growth.

Q3 revenue guided to $680-690M against $640.6M consensus, and a $590M cash acquisition of Stride Bank announced alongside. Raised 2026 to 26-27% sales growth and 17-18% EBITDA margins, with management pointing at $100M+ of net synergies and lower partner-bank costs.

Brent +2.96% to $100.82, its first print over $100 since July, and WTI +2.68% to $95.52. Fresh US strikes on Iranian tankers were answered by an Iranian missile barrage against a US facility in Jordan.
JPMorgan resumed at Overweight from Neutral with a $6 target, roughly 100% upside, citing execution confidence at Thacker Pass and lithium carbonate holding near $22.30/kg since mid-February.
bear: Third-quarter revenue guidance fell short of consensus, and that was enough to erase a Q2 revenue beat ($292.8M vs $285.9M) and a raised full-year revenue guide. The quarterly guide outweighed both.

A large FQ1 EPS beat at $7.37 against $6.77, but EBITDA of $485M only modestly cleared the $480M consensus and full-year guidance was merely reiterated. Investors took the 0.3% year-over-year decline in fuel sales and softer prepared-food comps instead.

Preannounced FQ3 operating income of just $115-175M against roughly $296M expected, citing fresh-pork spreads and lower hog prices. It follows a downside update from Tyson days earlier — a protein-complex problem rather than a company one.

Announced a €13B AI infrastructure investment in Finland. Capex commitments of that size have been read as margin pressure rather than growth this quarter, and it is the worst of the mega caps this morning.

Giving back part of Tuesday's move. It closed 104.47 after the Terafab foundry story, and premarket is fading it — the second-largest single-session gain in the Mag 11 this month now needs a second day to confirm.

darkpool.note: No FlowMS board has arrived for this session yet. Tuesday's grading stands as the last complete read, and it went the way the ask lean implied: the index complex printed ask for a third straight session into Friday — IVV $5.6B and SPY $5.4B cumulative — and SPY has now closed lower on both sessions since. The memory read from that board resolved as well: SNDK $5.1B and MU $5.0B, both mixed rather than bid, on the day they ripped 7% and 5%, and both have gone sideways-to-down since, with MU losing $1,000 Tuesday. This section updates when today's letter lands.

tts.label: Levels
tts.text: The levels that matter today. Meta, six twenty four eighty, Tuesday's failed high, already cleared by twenty dollars. U S O, one forty six twenty three. X L E, sixty five twenty four. Apple, three seventeen eighty six, and it stays broken below that, with the event at noon central rather than at the open. S P Y, seven sixty nine flat, which it lost on Tuesday and has not reclaimed, and premarket seven sixty three thirty one extends the break. Q Q Q printed an outside bar on Tuesday and the level is seven fifteen fifty seven on the downside, which premarket is already under. Oracle needs one sixty four eighty seven to resume, and it reports tomorrow after the close. ServiceTitan has no level at all, down nineteen percent on a quarterly guide despite beating on revenue and raising the full year. Two dated events sit inside this session. The Treasury announces the maximum size of its buyback operation at ten in the morning central, where the market wants a number well above the prior at least four billion, with some expecting ten billion or more. And Apple takes the stage at noon central. President Trump speaks at eight fifteen tonight.
